clue.text: Application rejected by copper — it's the drink!

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the short word for application is read backwards

parts.note: APP is the everyday short form of application, as on a phone

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a request from a policeman and declares that it is all about the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a police officer, but it is the metal, giving its chemical symbol. A cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuppa is a cup of tea, the classic British hot beverage, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Infatuation of female hugged by everybody in rocky bay

indicators.note: that combination sits inside the word for a bay

parts.note: a cove is a small sheltered bay, often rocky

indicators.note: the letter for female is hugged between the letters of the word for everybody

parts.note: all means everybody

explanation.surface: A young woman embraced by the whole crowd in a rugged little inlet: a teenage crush.
explanation.definitionFit: Calf love is the brief, intense romantic crush of a young person, an infatuation.

clue.text: Write piece about one being emperor, perhaps

parts.note: to pen is to write

indicators.note: the word for piece goes around the numeral for one

parts.note: piece is slang for a gun
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An instruction to write an article about someone who is emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: Emperor looks like a ruler, but it is the emperor penguin, the largest species; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The emperor is the largest kind of penguin, so the bird is defined by one of its species.

clue.text: Nails a GCSE after rejigging numbers

indicators.note: rejigging means rearranging, so the letters of these words are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pupil aces a school exam once the figures have been reworked.
explanation.walkthrough: Numbers is read as num-bers, things that numb: painkillers. A GCSE is the exam British pupils take at about sixteen.
explanation.definitionFit: Analgesics are painkilling drugs; they numb pain, so they are numbers in the sense of numbing agents.

clue.text: Chaos resulting from adjusting pH value across area

indicators.note: the rearranged letters stretch across the short form of area, which sits inside them
adjusting the letters of these words rearranges them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written: the seven letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A chemist warns that tinkering with the acidity of a whole region could lead to disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: An upheaval is a violent disturbance or upset, which amounts to disorder and confusion.

clue.text: Virtuous type calls to support withdrawing, using influence

indicators.note: in a down answer, the later pieces sit beneath and support the word for withdrawing

parts.note: pulling out means withdrawing
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a virtuous person
rings means telephones or calls

explanation.surface: A goody-goody phones to back out of something, trading on connections.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling strings means using one's influence or contacts secretly to get an advantage.

clue.text: Every pain after cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: Every bout of pain after a bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: Cycling suggests a bike ride, but here it means rotating the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Each and every both refer to all the members of a group taken individually.

clue.text: Ordinary article found in detached house

indicators.note: the article is found inside the word for a house

parts.note: a villa is a detached house, often in the suburbs
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A mundane item turns up in a stand-alone house.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla is used figuratively to mean plain, basic or unexciting, so it means ordinary.

clue.text: Fortunate, seeing game with leader getting red card

indicators.note: a red card sends a player off, so the first letter is sent off

parts.note: game means brave or plucky, as in game for anything

explanation.surface: A football match in which the captain is sent off, yet the team is lucky.
explanation.walkthrough: Game looks like a sport but is an adjective meaning spirited; in football, a red card sends a player off.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucky means favoured by chance, which is what fortunate means.

clue.text: Healthy walk within framework of the law

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stroll taken for one's health
second meaning: in line with a nation's constitution

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings run together as if the walk were legal; the noun and the adjective are the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a walk taken for exercise and an adjective for being in accordance with a constitution.

clue.text: In times past answer may be found in extended leave

indicators.note: says the abbreviation for answer sits within the other words

parts.note: long means extended in length or time
go is a verb meaning leave or depart

explanation.surface: Reads like a note that the reply to an old query is buried in a long period of absence.
explanation.walkthrough: A is the standard abbreviation for answer, as in Q and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Long ago means at a distant earlier time, so it is an adverb phrase equal to formerly.

clue.text: Short liberal American politician in charge

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, a member of the British political party

explanation.surface: A description of a brief, left-leaning American politician who is running things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like a description of the politician's height, but it is the definition, in the sense of brief in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic means using very few words, so speech that is terse or brief is short.

clue.text: Relax — clubs maybe will produce formal wear

parts.note: to lounge is to relax lazily
clubs is one of the four suits in a pack of cards, so this is a suit by example

explanation.surface: Taking it easy at golf or card clubs will somehow turn out smart clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounge suit is a man's matching jacket and trousers worn for business or semi-formal occasions.

clue.text: Scope for one of Shakespeare's works?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: freedom of movement, room to move
second meaning: a drama, such as Hamlet or Macbeth

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second meaning as an example: Shakespeare wrote poems too, but most of his works are dramas.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both slack or room for movement and a drama written for the stage.

clue.text: Measuring device for vehicle on farm

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
a tractor is the working vehicle of a farm

explanation.surface: A gauge designed for a farm vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A protractor is an instrument for measuring angles, a tool used in geometry.

clue.text: Cosmetic effect of the elite emigrating?

definitions.meaning: the literal sense: a skin product used as a make-up base
the joke sense: the best of society, the cream, disappearing abroad

explanation.walkthrough: The cream of society is its elite; if they all emigrated, that cream would be disappearing, which describes a type of face cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanishing cream is a light face moisturiser that is absorbed into the skin, leaving no greasy trace.

clue.text: 26 idiots speed periodically

parts.note: asses are fools

indicators.note: every other letter is taken, at regular intervals

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fools drive fast every now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: 26 Across is RATED; assessed means evaluated or judged, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: Ignores Conservatives, dropping international retail outlets

parts.note: to discount something is to disregard it

indicators.note: the Conservatives' nickname drops the letter for international

parts.note: Tories are members of the British Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A political complaint: someone brushes aside the Tories, who are abandoning international concerns.
explanation.definitionFit: Discount stores are shops selling goods cheaply, which makes them retail outlets.

clue.text: Vague idea of popular line adopted by monarch

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the letter for line is taken into the middle of the word for monarch

parts.note: a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A faint notion from a fashionable phrase that the king has taken up.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkling is a slight suspicion or hint, a vague idea.

clue.text: Torn about design for clothes

indicators.note: the word for torn goes around the word for design

parts.note: rent is an old past tense of rend, so it means torn
an aim is a design or purpose

explanation.surface: A ripped pattern intended for a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: Design suggests a dressmaking pattern, but it means intention.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is a literary word for clothing or garments.

clue.text: Symbol of life held by Tutankhamun

indicators.note: the answer is held within the letters of the pharaoh's name

parts.note: the pharaoh's name, read across its middle letters, carries the four-letter symbol

explanation.surface: An Egyptian life symbol in the grip of the boy pharaoh, as seen in tomb paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in the name, and the scene is apt: pharaohs are often shown holding this sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankh is the ancient Egyptian hieroglyph, a looped cross, standing for life.

clue.text: Writer showing a revolutionary attitude

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns over, so the word for attitude is turned backwards

parts.note: a pose is an attitude or stance

explanation.surface: An author with radical views.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek author of the famous fables.

clue.text: Losing power, imperialist moved to raise an army

indicators.note: the remaining letters are moved into a new order
the word imperialist loses the letter for power

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An empire-builder who has fallen from power decides to raise troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To militarise is to equip a nation with armed forces, building up its military strength.

clue.text: Pack exhibit, needing time for hotel

indicators.note: the word for exhibit needs a change of one letter
the letter for time takes the place of the letter for hotel

parts.note: to show is to exhibit

explanation.surface: Packing up an exhibition, needing time before getting to the hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: In the phonetic alphabet, H is Hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow is to pack or store something away neatly.

clue.text: Hand in one by the first of September, being struck?

indicators.note: the first letter is placed beside the next piece
only the opening letter of September is taken

parts.note: only its opening letter is used
a mitten is a glove with a hand inside it, so one with a hand in it is a mitten

explanation.surface: A hand is raised in a vote by the start of September, with someone getting hit?
explanation.walkthrough: Hand in one is a cryptic way to describe a mitten. The question mark flags that struck means struck by love, not by a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Smitten means struck with love or infatuation, so being struck fits in that sense.

clue.text: Drains, say, in case of gas

indicators.note: the word for say goes inside those outer letters
the case of a word is its outside, so only the first and last letters of gas

parts.note: only the two outside letters of the word are used
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: Domestic plumbing worry: drains in the event of a gas problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drains, say' looks like one phrase, but the comma splits them: drains is the definition, say is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutters are channels that carry rainwater away, so they are drains.

clue.text: Who's going to take in kitchen waste?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, split as two words: the farmyard animals are the ones who will eat it
second meaning: food scraps fed to farm animals

explanation.walkthrough: The question 'Who's going to take in kitchen waste?' is answered by splitting the answer as PIGS WILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigswill is leftover food and kitchen scraps given to pigs as feed.

clue.text: Time taken in returning expensive 16 Down

indicators.note: the letter for time is taken inside the other word
the word for expensive is read backwards

parts.note: dear means costly

explanation.surface: Reads like a note about a costly item coming back with time absorbed.
explanation.definitionFit: 16 Down is ASSESSED; rated means evaluated or judged, a synonym.
